title: Flash sale: absorb the reads, gate the writes
brief: Design ticket sales for a huge concert, or a sneaker drop. Reads are people loading the event page and seat map; writes are buy attempts. Buy attempts must go to the primary database so nothing is oversold.

requirements: The event page can be a few seconds stale
variants.twist: Bots arrive: spike(multiplier=3, seconds=20). Which layer takes the hit, and what would you put in front of it?

requirements: Most buyers will get 'sold out' anyway: up to 30% of all requests may be turned away
p99 < 300 ms for the requests you accept
variants.twist: Rejected buyers retry instantly, and bots retry fastest. How would a waiting room (a queue with positions and tokens) change who gets a pair?

hints: Which requests must reach the database, and which could be answered from a copy?
A CDN answers most page reads at the edge, and a cache takes the reads that get through. Buy attempts still hit one primary at about 5k/s. If they come in at 3x that, who gets turned away, and where?

Onsale: put two layers in front of the database that answer reads, one at the edge and one in front of the DB, and size the services for what gets past them. Drop: the primary takes about 5k writes/s. Cap buy attempts below that before they reach the services.
_notes: Onsale: no CDN needs ~60 services and the DB still collapses. CDN (0.9) alone: DB gets 4.75k reads + 2.5k writes (rho 1.45), fails. CDN + cache 0.9 + 10 services: DB rho 0.89 (mostly the 2.5k writes), p99 ~53 ms, $1.78. CDN + 2 read replicas passes ($2.63, over budget). Drop: CDN + 20 services: 15k writes collapse the DB. CDN -> gateway 4000 -> 6 services: p99 ~60 ms, 21% errors, $1.28; a 6000 limit overloads the DB (rho 1.2). CockroachDB with 18 nodes takes it all but costs $5.44. The sim has no hot-row lock on the one product; in Postgres every buyer updates the same inventory row. Ask how they'd avoid that (pre-split stock into buckets, Redis DECR, reservations with expiry). Checked in frontend/src/lessons/content.test.ts.
